Piri 是韓國的雙簧氣鳴樂器，用於民間音樂與古典宮廷音樂。其主體為竹製管身，採: The piri is a Korean double-reed aerophone used in folk music and in classical court music. Its body is a bamboo tube with a cylindrical bore, drilled with fingerholes; the typical layout has eight holes, seven at the front and one at the back for the thumb, and it carries a large double reed. It is usually played sitting upright, chin slightly drawn in and back straight to allow good breathing, holding the tube with both hands and taking the mouthpiece into the mouth.
Piri 用於韓國民間音樂與古典（宮廷）音樂。鄉 Piri 因響亮且帶鼻音，通常: The piri is used in Korean folk music and in classical (court) music. The hyang piri is loud and nasal and normally carries the melody in an ensemble; the se piri is quieter and suits use with voices or soft string instruments. The dang piri has a wider body and resembles the Chinese guanzi. The modernised North Korean dae piri has keys and a bell added and looks close to the Western oboe; the bass piri uses clarinet-style keys, lies in the low register and was developed in 1962. These types show that the instrument can appear in court music, in folk ensembles, as vocal accompaniment and in the playing of modernised instruments.
Piri為韓國雙簧氣鳴樂器，起源中亞，經中國傳入朝鮮半島，三國時期高句麗、百濟已: The piri is a Korean double-reed aerophone that originated in Central Asia and reached the Korean peninsula through China; it was already in use in Goguryeo and Baekje during the Three Kingdoms period. The Suishu says it was also called gagwan and came from Kucha (now in Xinjiang). In the reign of Yejong of Goryeo another double-reed cylindrical instrument came in from Song China, and to tell them apart the older instrument was called hyangpiri and the newcomer dangpiri. The sepiri is smaller but has the same construction and range, and appeared later. The modernised North Korean daepiri has keys and a bell; the jeo piri uses clarinet-style keys, lies in the double-bass register and took shape in 1962. Its Chinese counterpart is the guan (also called bili) and its Japanese counterpart the hichiriki.

The sounding element is a large double reed. The source does not state the reed's material, nor the materials of the keys, bell and other parts on the modernised types, so all that can be confirmed is that the main materials are bamboo and a double reed.

觱篥是一種雙簧管樂器，音色明亮刺激，具有穿透力強的特徵。其音質帶有濃厚的民族特色: The piri is a double-reed instrument with a bright, exciting timbre that carries strongly. Its tone has a strong national character: it does not lose warmth, yet carries a subtle huskiness. The range is wide and it can play the middle and upper register, where the timbre is especially sharp and bright.
觱篥的共鳴主要依靠管身內部的音孔設計，產生獨特的諧波結構，使其音響具有層次感。相: The piri resonates mainly through the design of the fingerholes in the body, which produces a distinctive harmonic structure and gives its sound layers. Compared with the Western oboe, the piri's timbre has more of an Eastern flavour and a warm folk-music air; compared with the crispness of the flute it has more weight and force. Its timbre is very recognisable in an ensemble and is often used to bring out a national style and dramatic tension.
